title: classList add/remove vs rewriting className
variable: classList mutation vs className string rewrite
claim: perf-lint.ts lists 'CSSTOM vs string style updates' among the patterns it deliberately cannot check, because both techniques leave identical DOM state and so have no structural trace to detect. That makes this measurable only here. The practical question is whether rewriting className - which replaces every class rather than mutating one - forces more style work than a targeted classList call.
result: NOT CONFIRMED. No reliable difference at 30, 100 or 300 on any phase. Rewriting the whole className string costs no more than a targeted classList call in cohtml. Worth reading alongside csstext-vs-property-writes, which DID find a 2-3.5x penalty for rebuilding style.cssText as a string: the engine evidently treats a class-attribute rewrite cheaply while a style-declaration string has to be parsed. The web lumps these two together as string-building antipatterns; in Gameface only one of them is real.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. classList is not covered by the feature inventory at all, so it was verified manually against the Player: add, remove, contains and toggle(name, force) all work. Rule 1: one variable, the API used to change the class. Rule 2: identical DOM and identical CSS. Rule 3: identical JS apart from the single USE_CLASSLIST constant; both pages define both mutation paths. Rule 4: no text, no assets. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the class churn IS the case and replaces the shared damage driver; every tile changes class every frame from load in both variants. Rule 7: the on/off state derives from the frame counter and the tile index. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is Styles. NOTE: both variants end each frame in the same DOM state and repaint the same pixels, so any difference is attributable to the mutation path rather than to what got rendered.
